title: Control of Mexican poppy in Tef

Header: Control of Mexican poppy in Tef

Prevention: Use certified clean seed for growing crops; seeds considered as the main means of spread
Clean farm machinery and tools after leaving an affected area to reduce the risk of spread
Remove weed before making hay, grain or other animal feed
Do not allow livestock to graze on sparse pasture where weed is present.
Livestock otherwise may eat the poisonous weed
Monitoring: A short-lived (i.e. annual) herbaceous plant initially forming a basal rosette of leaves, then later developing upright (i.e. erect) stems.
Flowers are creamy white to yellow, on a short stalk.
Sepals are sparsely prickled with a large spine just below the apex
Check fields for infestation every two weeks and take direct control measures when found
Check for flowering every two weeks and consider management to prevent seed set, spread and build up of seed bank
Direct Control: Hand pulling at early growth stage.
Wear hand gloves if the plant develops spines
Control the plant well before harvest as control at a later growth stage is costly and causes high crop loss
Remove the weed before flowering to avoid buildup of seed bank
Restrictions: Use of chemical herbicides may lead to the development of herbicide resistance.
When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label, such as dosage
Post-emergence application of 2,4-D (72%) at rate of 1
Pyroxsulam (45%) at rate of 400 mL/ha to control the weed
